newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia Air delays releasing passenger list.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia Air delays releasing passenger list.

text.p: Ethiopian Airlines said on Sunday it would not issue a passenger list from the hijacked plane that crashed into the sea near the Comoro Islands until final identification of the dead was complete.

"This is a serious matter. We have to be certain about those who have lost their lives and those who have survived before we issue a statement," said Ethiopian Airlines general manager Ahmed Kello. He declined to say when the list would be issued.
At least 67 bodies have been recovered from the Boeing 767 flight ET 961 that crashed after it ran out of fuel. Fifty-two people survived and 56 are missing presumed dead.
Nationals of twenty-four countries were represented among the non-transit passengers who boarded at the Ethiopian capital.
These included 18 Ethiopians, eight Kenyans, eight Israelis, seven British, four Ukrainians, four French, three Italians, two Cameroonians, two Djiboutians, two Swedish and two Americans.
There was one passenger each from Austria, Canada, Congo, Germany, Hungary, India, Japan, Korea, Lesotho, Somalia, Switzerland, Uganda and Yemen.

Transit passenger who arrived in Addis from other flights included 18 Indians, 16 Nigerians, 10 Malians, six Sri Lankans, two Americans, two Kenyans, two Liberians and one each from Pakistan, Benin, Zaire, Congo, Ivory Coast, Chad, Sierra Leone and Belgium.
